title: High-consequence subsystem rewrite proposed for structural cleanliness
task: Review a proposal to replace a long-lived patient-record module with a clean rewrite because the current structure violates preferred layering.
context: The module handles persisted patient data and critical workflows.
The current implementation is difficult to navigate but stable in production.
The proposed rewrite has no complete characterization suite.
No staged migration or rollback plan exists.
evidence: Recent incidents are not caused by the current layering.
Existing tests cover only a subset of externally observable behavior.
The rewrite motivation is primarily architectural cleanliness.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Approve the rewrite because the target architecture is cleaner.
Replace the whole module before adding more tests because tests would encode legacy design.
expected_decision_properties: Raise the evidence and verification threshold because failure consequences are high.
Reject architectural cleanliness alone as sufficient rewrite justification.
Require stronger behavioral characterization and a migration/cutover/rollback strategy before replacement.
Allow targeted risk-reducing refactors if they can be verified independently.
unacceptable_reasoning: Old code should be rewritten when it is hard to read.
High-consequence code benefits from big-bang cleanup because partial modernization is messy.
Tests are optional if the new architecture is simpler.
verification_expectations: Build characterization/contract coverage for critical behavior.
Exercise migration and rollback using representative persisted data.
Compare old/new behavior for critical workflows before cutover.
specialist_boundary: Domain-specific clinical/safety correctness requires appropriate specialist validation.
